quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How can you help reduce road rage?

options.text: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.
Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Use your horn often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, follow all traffic laws, signs, signals, and road markings. Always signal before you change lanes.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding or driving too fast for the conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Looking around and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding or driving too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving above the speed limit or driving too fast for current conditions are major causes of traffic crashes. Always drive at safe speeds within the legal limit.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must let you go first.
Never let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic going straight. You must always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and keep your speed the same.
Speed up to get past them quickly.
Slow down and pass carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and pass carefully.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who might cross in front of you. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What should a driver do?

options.text: Look straight ahead only.
Focus only on the center of the road.
Watch all around your car—front, sides, and back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch all around your car—front, sides, and back.
questions.explanation: A good driver watches what is happening on all sides of their vehicle. Always be aware of everything around you.

questions.question: Is it legal to drive if medication affects your driving?

options.text: Never.
Yes, if you don't feel sleepy.
Yes, if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while impaired by any substance. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: How can you spot an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden, unsafe lane changes.
By how many passengers are in their car.
By their tendency to drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden, unsafe lane changes.
questions.explanation: Pay attention to other drivers. If you notice a driver making sudden or unsafe lane changes, do not challenge them. The safest choice is to stay away from them.

questions.question: What are speeding fines in work zones?

options.text: They can be double the normal fine amount.
They are usually not enforced.
You can argue them in court.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can be double the normal fine amount.
questions.explanation: In Connecticut, speeding in a work zone can result in fines up to $1,000, points on your license, and a required driver retraining course. Using a cell phone in a work zone doubles the fine.

questions.question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave at you first.
Only if the pedestrians are not using their phone.
Always.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk for any pedestrian. You may go only when your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: What can happen if you take prescription medication and drink alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
You will be more alert.
You may not be able to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not be able to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect your driving ability. They are especially dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: To see better in rain or fog, drivers should use their:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beams reflect off water and precipitation, making it harder to see.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Closer behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.
Farther behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay farther behind a large truck because trucks have larger blind spots where the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: After passing another vehicle, you should return to your original lane only when you:

options.text: Beep your horn.
See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
Flash your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Look for both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This means you have enough space to safely return to your original lane.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?

options.text: Breathe in fresh air.
Wait for time to pass.
Drink coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for time to pass.
questions.explanation: Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol content. Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your body.

questions.question: You want to turn right at a corner. A pedestrian with a guide dog is crossing in front of you. You should:

options.text: Turn off your engine until the person crosses.
Tell the pedestrian when to cross.
Wait until the person crosses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the person crosses.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes always have the right-of-way. You must let them cross before turning.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green protected turn is ending. You must prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness.
Coordination.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many driving skills. These include reaction time, coordination, alertness, and the ability to concentrate.

questions.question: The best way to change lanes is:

options.text: Quickly and often.
When a car is in your blind spot.
Slowly and carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and carefully. Change lanes only when needed. Every lane change increases the risk of an accident.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep extra space between your car and barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Do not tailgate.

questions.question: As you enter a roundabout, you should slow down and:

options.text: Yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing.
Yield to cars already in the roundabout.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and all traffic already inside the roundabout.

questions.question: What information do blue traffic signs provide?

options.text: Motorist services.
Construction and maintenance.
Mileage information and distances to specific locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorist services.
questions.explanation: Blue signs are service signs. They tell drivers where to find services like rest areas, food, or hospitals.

questions.question: Why are work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs used?

options.text: To make drivers angry about slow traffic.
To inconvenience drivers.
To keep traffic out of dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep traffic out of dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Look for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests to warn you of hazards ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on the upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and be ready to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: What is a crosswalk?

options.text: Another name for a four-way intersection.
An area designated for construction workers.
The area where pedestrians can cross the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The area where pedestrians can cross the road.
questions.explanation: Crosswalks are shown by white lines to mark where pedestrians cross. Some crosswalks are marked with lines. Others may not be marked at all.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing warning lights?

options.text: Drive around the crossing gates if you don't see a train.
Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates lift.
Slow down and drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop well behind the gates, wait for the tracks to clear, then proceed when the gates lift.
questions.explanation: You must stop at railroad crossings with warning signs or flashing lights. It is illegal to drive around lowered gates.
